newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt to advise ministers on 98 spending cap.
newsitem.headline: French govt to advise ministers on 98 spending cap.

text.p: The French government will send on Wednesday or Thursday letters to ministries outlining their spending caps ahead of the introduction of the 1998 budget, government sources said on Tuesday.

One source said it would be "surprising" if the letters included a 1997 public deficit target of three percent of Gross Domestic Product as required under the Maastricht treaty criteria for joining a single European currency from 1999.
Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has commissioned an audit of public finances, which is expected to show that the 1997 deficit exceeds the three percent threshold, the sources said.
Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn told parliament earlier in the day that the audit was likely to show a bigger than expected deficit this year.
But he said Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's government would balance any spending commitments by foregoing other expenditure it would otherwise like to have undertaken.
Strauss-Kahn said those carrying out the audit would present their findings on July 21.
In a June 24 letter to the auditors, Jospin said he wanted to give a new direction to France's economic policy but would keep in mind the need to reduce deficits.
"The government is determined to steer France's economic policy towards growth, employment and national solidarity, while keeping in mind (the need to) reduce public deficits," Jospin wrote.
